name: Linear thermal expansion (CTE) of borosilicate glasses LK5 and Borofloat 33 from 130 K to 800 K by push-rod thermomechanical analysis
plain_name: Measure how much a glass shrinks and grows between -143 C and 526 C
description: 20 mm glass samples stand under a quartz push-rod probe (0.2 N) in a thermomechanical analyser; the chamber is pre-cooled and then heated at 10 K/min from about 130 K to 800 K while the length change is logged; CTE polynomials are fitted for anodic silicon-glass bonding (MEMS) design.
keywords: Measure how much a glass shrinks and grows between -143 C and 526 C

sources.citation: Sinev L. S., Petrov I. D. Linear thermal expansion coefficient (at temperatures from 130 to 800 K) of borosilicate glasses applicable for coupling with silicon in microelectronics. Steklo i Keramika 2016 no.1 35-38; Glass and Ceramics 73 (2016) 32-35, doi:10.1007/s10717-016-9820-0 (arXiv:1801.01181)

requirements.rationale: The CTE data set covers 130 K to 800 K; the sample space must span both ends.
20 mm long samples stand on the pedestal under the vertical push rod, so the usable length along the loading axis must be at least 20 mm.
Optional: the heating run was made at 10 K/min.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
